And Another on 10 March, 2025 High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:34515 Court No. - 77 Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 7824 of 2025 Applicant :- Arun Dwivedi Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Diksha Kesarwani,Umesh Chandra Kesarwani Counsel for Opposite Party :- Abhinava Krishna Srivastava,G.A. Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J. 1. Heard Sri Umesh Chandra Krsarwani, learned counsel for the applicant; Sri Abhinava Krishna Srivastava, learned counsel for opposite party No.2 and Sri Sandeep Chaudhary, learned A.G.A for the State. 2. The instant application has been filed seeking quashing of the entire proceeding of complaint case No. 5166 of 2011, under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, P.S. Barra, District Kanpur Nagar as well as summoning order dated 28.6.2019. 3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the impugned proceeding is absolutely malicious and, therefore, the same is bad in the eyes of law. 4. However, learned counsel for opposite party No.2 has raised a preliminary objection that the applicant has already approached this Court against the impugned proceeding through application u/s 482 No. 43431 of 2012 which was disposed of along with a bunch of cases on 13.4.2016.

texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the impugned proceeding is absolutely malicious and, therefore, the same is bad in the eyes of law. 4. However, learned counsel for opposite party No.2 has raised a preliminary objection that the applicant has already approached this Court against the impugned proceeding through application u/s 482 No. 43431 of 2012 which was disposed of along with a bunch of cases on 13.4.2016. Therefore, the present application is not maintainable as the ground raised by the applicant in the Arun Dwivedi vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165295546/ 1 present case was available to him while filing the earlier application. 5. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant submits that he does not want to press the prayer for quashing of the proceedings. Applicant wants to surrender before the court below and apply for bail. He further submits that this Court may be pleased to direct the court concerned to consider the bail application of the applicant expeditiously within stipulated period of time as may be fixed by this Court. The investigating agencies and their officers are duty-bound to comply with the mandate of Sections 41 and 41-A of the Code and the directions issued by this Court in Arnesh Kumar [Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273 : (2014) 3 SCC (Cri) 449]. There needs to be a strict compliance of the mandate laid down in the judgment of this Court in Siddharth [Siddharth v. State of U.P., (2022) 1 SCC 676 : (2022) 1 SCC (Cri) 423]. 100.7. An exercise will have to be done in a similar manner to comply with the mandate of Section 436-A of the Code both at the district judiciary level and the High Court as earlier directed by this Court in Bhim Singh [Bhim Singh v. Union of India, (2015) 13 SCC 605 : (2016) 1 SCC (Cri) 663] , followed by appropriate orders. Bail applications ought to be disposed of within a period of two weeks except if the provisions mandate otherwise, with the exception being an intervening application. 8. It is needless to mention that the Apex Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs Central Bureau of Investigation and another; (2021) 10 SCC 773 has also approved for grant of interim bail till disposal of bail application. Para 6 of the Satender Kumar Antil (supra) decided on 07.10.2021 is being quoted as under: "6.
